correctness.rationale: With the stated matrix and basis, the three Fourier sectors have eigenvalues 0, plus/minus sqrt3 and reduced matrices [[lambda,1],[1,0]]. Exponentiating those exact 2x2 matrices gives the displayed mixed-layer kernel. The elementary triangle inequality proves an upper bound (1+4/sqrt7)/3. Q-linear independence of 1, sqrt3 and sqrt7 proves dense positive Kronecker flow and therefore sharpness for every cyclic offset. Simultaneous equality of two sine factors at finite time would rationalize sqrt7, proving strict nonattainment. Independent numerical full-matrix reconstruction checks all nine amplitudes at seven times and 4500 further instances; computations are corroborative and the proof is infinite.

originality.rationale: Targeted scientific-record and exact-phrase literature searches, plus material inspection of the two papers treating the identical graph, revealed no explicit or more general sharp cross-layer site-pair supremum. Bottarelli et al. treat exterior-to-exterior routing and superposition channels. Acuaviva et al. classify non-pendant-to-non-pendant PGST and give spectral projector ingredients, not the mixed core-to-pendant maximum. The new contribution is the exact all-time optimizer supremum, its equality across nine mixed channels, and the arithmetic nonattainment theorem. An independently written equivalent optimization remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The six-site geometry is an explicit quantum routing device in the primary physical source. Its established nearly ideal external-to-external routing might invite the inference that internal-to-external single-vertex conversion is similarly high-fidelity. The theorem gives a sharp contrary hardware restriction: no time yields fidelity above about 0.7010478, at any of the nine internal/external pairs. This answers a natural exact channel-performance question for the same device, with a universal 29.9% unavoidable failure at fixed parameters. It does not overstate to arbitrary detuning, flux, encodings or speed.
